attributes.body_ja:
「ところ」で説明（せつめい）したように、「ところ」は、動詞（どうし）が過去形（かこけい）でない場合（ばあい）に、「これから (A) が起（お）こりそうだ」という状況（じょうきょう）を表（あらわ）す名詞（めいし）です。この「ところ」が「だった」に付（つ）くと、(A) が起（お）こる直前（ちょくぜん）だったが、実際（じっさい）には起（お）こらなかった（またはそのときにもっと重要（じゅうよう）な出来事（できごと）が起（お）こった）ことを表（あらわ）します。

「ところ」に付（つ）く動詞（どうし）は、助動詞（じょどうし）「ない」が付（つ）いて否定形（ひていけい）になることもあります。この場合（ばあい）、「(A) は起（お）こらないはずだったが、結果的（けっかてき）に起（お）こった」という意味（いみ）になります。
attributes.body:
As explained in the ところ grammar point, ところ is a noun that is often used to highlight the situation within which a verb is 'about to' happen (when that verb appears in its non-past form). However when followed by だった, it emphasizes that the thing that was 'about to' happen never actually eventuated (or that another more important event happened at that moment). This can be translated as 'to almost (A)', or 'to be on the verge of (A)'.

The verb that ところ is paired with may also be seen grouped with the auxiliary verb ない. In this case, it implies that something was 'about not' to happen (but then did).

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: ところだった can be used with two closely related nuances. The more literal meaning expresses the idea of 'was just about to (A)', as in: 昼ご飯を食べるところだった ('I was just about to eat lunch.'). The more figurative meaning conveys that something nearly happened but ultimately didn't, similar to 'I almost (A)' or 'I nearly (A)' in English, as in: 死ぬところだった ('I almost died' [but didn't]).

attributes.body: るところだ and ところだった① both express that an action is or was about to happen, but differ in outcome. るところだ means the action is about to occur and likely will. ところだった① means it was on the verge of happening, but didn't in the end.
